claims.text: Calling toString on an Output<T> in Pulumi produces placeholder text of the form `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, which can appear in a log line, a generated file, or a resource property instead of the expected value.
A page titled 'Output value errors' exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ and covers this and other symptoms of treating a Pulumi output as if it were already a plain value.
A troubleshooting page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ covering errors from stringifying, branching on, or reading a Pulumi output value like a plain value.
In Pulumi programs, stringifying, branching on, or reading an Output value as if it were a plain value produces errors.
A troubleshooting page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ for "409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress" errors from Pulumi Cloud.
Pulumi Cloud can return 500 internal server errors.

The page /docs/iac/operations/stack-management/using-a-diy-backend/ has an anchor #error-reading-pulumimetayaml covering `read ".pulumi/meta.yaml"` errors when the CLI can't access a self-managed state backend.
Crashes or hangs on Apple Silicon can be caused by x86_64 binaries running under Rosetta 2.
A recently deleted Pulumi stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`.
The Pulumi CLI supports `--target` and `--exclude` flags to limit operations to specific resources.
Pulumi provides automatic logging, CLI verbose logging, and program logging for debugging and diagnostics.
Pulumi offers pre-release dev builds that include bug fixes that haven't shipped in a stable release yet.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends the logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team.
The logging guide at /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/ has an 'automatic-logging' anchor section.
The verbose logging content is at /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/#cli-verbose-logging.
`pulumi destroy` can fail in some scenarios, covered by the destroy-failures page.
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values because their real values are not known until the resource providing them has been created or updated.

When an Output is converted to a string directly (concatenated or logged) instead of via apply or an equivalent helper, Pulumi does not raise an error by default but silently substitutes a placeholder message for the value.
In TypeScript, converting an Output to a string produces literal text such as `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate`.
In TypeScript, calling `JSON.stringify()` on an Output, or letting one flow into a JSON body, produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value.
In Python, formatting an Output into a string produces literal text such as `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported`, and Pulumi also logs a warning.
In Python, passing an Output to `json.dumps()` fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`.
In Python, `Output.json_dumps()` is the way to serialize an Output to JSON.
In Go, passing a `pulumi.StringOutput` where a `string` is expected is a compile error.
In Go, values are resolved inside `ApplyT`.
In C#, converting an Output to a string produces literal text such as `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format`.
Setting the environment variable `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` makes converting an Output to a string throw an exception instead of returning placeholder text, in TypeScript, Python, and C#.
When Output-to-string conversion yields placeholder text, the program runs and `pulumi up` succeeds.

String-composition helpers for Outputs are `pulumi.interpolate` and `pulumi.concat` in TypeScript, `Output.concat`/`Output.format`/`Output.json_dumps` in Python, `pulumi.Sprintf`/`pulumi.JSONMarshal` in Go, and `Output.Format` in C#.
The `apply` callback runs asynchronously once the output resolves, generally after the program's top-level code has finished running.
Most resource inputs accept Outputs as well as plain values.
A resource's logical name is a position that cannot accept an Output.
In a dynamically typed language, an `if` on an Output evaluates the Output object rather than its eventual value and is generally always true.
In a statically typed language, branching on an `Output<bool>` is usually a compile error because an `Output<bool>` is not a `bool`.
A stack configuration setting read with `pulumi.Config`, an environment variable, or a hardcoded flag is a plain value that can be branched on directly.
Passing an Output as a resource's logical name or loop bound or map key fails to compile in TypeScript, Go, and C#.
In Python, passing an Output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Python, using an Output as a loop bound (`range(some_output)`) raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Python, using an Output as a dictionary key does not raise; Python falls back to comparing and hashing the Output object itself.
A StackReference lets a later, separate stack consume the first stack's outputs.

Pulumi has no supported way to block the program and read a resolved value out of an Output synchronously; awaiting or reading it synchronously either doesn't compile, fails at runtime, or returns placeholder text.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output after a deployment.
The Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update (for example `res.Outputs` in Go).

Cross-referenced pages exist: /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/#outputs, /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply/, /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/all/, /docs/iac/concepts/stacks/#stackreferences, /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/.
